svg.title: AssignEmptyTrayToMove: which empty tray?
svg.desc: A READY_FOR_INSERT job asked for 'an empty tray into bay B21' without saying which. This helper searches outward from the bay for the nearest tray without a payload and writes its id into the event.
svg.metadata: ["Start: the request arrives. The map is working_state as the method first sees it; no events yet. Step through the method one table row at a time.", "Row 1. An empty-tray move must at least say where the tray should go. Without a destination there is nothing to search from. In this example: dest = {node_id: 21, heading: -90}, the bay's inbound pose (heading 90, faces_reciprocal: true). (passes)", "Row 2. The search starts at the destination and grows outward, because the question is 'which empty tray is closest to where it is needed?'. In this example: Start vertex = the one for {node_id: 21, heading: -90}. (start = B21)", "Row 3. Build the graph filter for a tray footprint with every tray and AGV left out, so occupied nodes do not stop the search; only disabled or static obstacles do. In this example: All six trays and every AGV are left out of the filter. (filter)", "Row 4. Run the search. The environment's goal is a node that holds a tray with no payload. Each edge costs its trapezoid time plus 30 s for every tray it crosses, so a near tray behind blockers can lose to a farther one. In this example: Reached in order: W41, W22, then W25, W18 and P23. P23 holds T23, which carries no car. (found P23)", "Row 5. If no empty tray is reachable, the whole tray assignment fails with this message. In this example: A tray was found. (skipped)", "Row 6. Take the tray on the node the search reached and write its id into the existing event. The event object is edited in place; nothing is added to the DAG. In this example: The event now reads T23: P23 -> B21. (tray = 23)", "Row 7. Avoid a pointless rotation: if the tray already sits on the same axis as the destination heading, keep the tray's heading. In this example: T23 faces 90, the destination asks for 90: nothing to change. (no change)", "Row 8. Return. AssignTrays then treats the event like any other complete move and runs the blocking-tray loop for it. In this example: Next: the blocking-tray loop for T23's path to B21 (P23 -> W22 -> W41 -> B21). (success)", "Playing the plan (one illustrative execution: AGV assignment and motion planning choose the real AGV and route): AGV-1 drives empty W27 -> W26 -> P23 and stops under T23 (the approach for event 2; AGV assignment adds such moves later).", "Playing the plan: event 2. AGV-1 lifts T23, carries it P23 -> W22 -> W41 -> B21 and lowers it. Every tray and AGV is now where the plan leaves it."]
